m3_seq_v5.evidence: build() only loads m3_seq_{full,big,s1}.pt; the only training path (m3_seq_v1.get_net/train_net) uses the train dict, and nothing in systems/ or tune/ trains GRUs on val/test. tune/m3_tune.py reads bench3.eval_sets('val') to pick the 5 voice-leading weights (stated as 'val-tuned'), but test reproduces val: val 0.7199, test 0.7197 (scored with bench3.score directly, board not written). Causality probe: 72 cuts on 24 val songs, randomizing every later pitch, the durations from note i on, and all chord labels -> outputs 0..i identical in 72/72. Running songs in reverse order changes nothing, so no state carries across songs. DUET_HIST=4: changing notes outside the window changed later outputs in 6/47 probes, but always only after Duet's own earlier note had changed (voice-leading cost on self.prev), never through the melody window itself, so that is fine. Speed 130-200 us/note.

m3_seq_v4.evidence: Same code path as v5 (Ens of full+big GRUs, val-tuned VL weights). Causality 72/72 clean, no order dependence. Test 0.7139 vs val 0.7142. 90-150 us/note.

m5_policy_v9.evidence: build() trains or loads models_m5/m5_<md5>.npz keyed on train-set sizes (bach 135, folk 511, pop 8149, pop909 322 = bench3.train_sets) and P. make_rows uses only the train dict, and its targets use true chords from train songs only. NoteState only uses finished notes (prev_dur given), beats before floor(onset), and the current pitch. Per-song memory is reset in start(). Causality 72/72 clean, no order dependence. DUET_HIST=4: 2/47 differences, both only through Duet's own previous note. Test 0.7125 vs val 0.7137. ~95 us/note. Caveat: doubling is 0.23-0.25 on every set (test bach 0.247), right at the 0.25 DOUBLING cut, because wd was tuned to sit just under it.

m5_policy_v12.evidence: Same model as v9 (tag v9, same npz), only vl 0.003. No leakage: causality 72/72 clean, no order dependence, no eval data read. But on test its bach doubling is 0.251 > 0.25, so bench3 would flag it DOUBLING and leave it unranked on test. Its val rank (0.7134) comes from doubling tuned to the edge of the cut, not from better harmony. Test headline 0.7134.

bench_issues: Doubling pays off in 'music': a unison or octave counts as consonant, so whenever her note is a chord tone, doubling it is a sure hit. The only guard is the binary 25% DOUBLING flag, and the m5 systems are tuned to 0.23-0.25 (v12 test bach 0.251). Compare at matched doubling, or leave unison/octave out of 'music', before ranking m5 against m3 (doubling 0.08-0.18).

Silent time counts in the denominators of harsh, double and inkey but adds nothing to them. A system could stay under the DOUBLING/harsh limits by singing silence. It does not inflate 'music' (silent time counts against music on labeled beats), and none of the top 4 ever returns -1.
Beats with no chord label (z<0) are left out of fit/music. They are only 0.0-1.6% of scored singing time (pop highest), and a system cannot tell which beats they are, so the inflation is negligible.

The headline is the plain mean of 4 datasets, but bach val is only 17 songs / ~1056 notes (test 27). So 25% of the headline rests on ~1k notes, and the top-4 val spread (0.006) is within that noise. The m3_seq_v5 lead does hold on test (0.720 vs 0.713-0.714).

board() keeps the MAX headline per system name, and evaluate() does not record the environment (DUET_HIST, DUET_M5, M3_*, M3_TAG), even though these change behaviour under the same name. Rerunning with tuned env vars quietly picks the best run on val. Also, m3_seq_*.pt and the models_m5 caches are regenerated or overwritable, so older board rows may not be reproducible. Log the env and a checkpoint hash.

Voice-leading weights for m3_seq_v3/v4/v5 and the wd/vl knobs for m5 were tuned on val, and val is also what the board reports. Test scores (computed here without writing the board) agree within 0.002, so no material overfitting, but the board should show test for its final ranking.
DUET_HIST limits the melody history only. Systems still condition on their own previous output (voice-leading), which carries older information. This is reasonable, but the docs should say so.
Small train/eval duplicates by identical melody: val folk 1, val pop 1, test folk 1, test pop 2. Negligible.
